summary: This Deskera blog article is a general guide to wood manufacturing, covering types of processes (sawing, planing, drilling, shaping, sanding, finishing), benefits, wood selection and grading, sustainable practices, treatments and finishes, the evolution toward CNC and digital fabrication, industry challenges, and future trends. It closes by promoting Deskera's MRP, ERP, Books, CRM and People software for inventory and production management.
one_line: A Deskera blog guide to the wood manufacturing process, covering techniques, wood grading, sustainability, technology trends, industry challenges, and Deskera software.
key_facts: The article is titled 'Wood Manufacturing Process: A Complete Guide' and was written by Rhema Hans.
Wood manufacturing is described as transforming raw lumber into products or components of a larger product.
Sawing can be done by hand but most often is done with a sawmill using circular saws, bandsaws, or chainsaws.
Planing is done by running wood through a planer, which removes small amounts of wood at a time to make it smooth and even.
The article states the primary benefit of wood manufacturing is that it is a sustainable and renewable resource.
The article recommends hardwoods for furniture and cabinetry, while softwoods are better suited for farming or construction.

Sustainable practices listed include sourcing materials certified by the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) and using equipment certified by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's Energy Star program.
The article recommends water-based finishes because they can help reduce VOCs (Volatile Organic Compounds) and hazardous waste.
Wood treatments discussed include preservatives, fire retardants, fungicides, and waterproofing agents.
The article names computer numerical control (CNC) technology as a major advancement that allows faster production and higher accuracy.
Challenges listed include rising raw material costs, environmental regulations, increased competition from plastic and metal manufacturing, and labor shortages.
The future section cites automation, renewable resources such as bamboo and cork, 3D printing, laser cutting, and digital fabrication as trends.
Deskera MRP lets users control production schedules, compile a Bill of Materials, produce reports, and build dashboards.
Deskera People is described as a tool for centralizing human resource management, including payroll processing, overtime, benefits, bonuses, and training programs.
